scope: Existing israel-knesset-channel linear Channel99 programme guide; no committee-room mixing or playback/rights change

primary_evidence.finding: The broadcaster identifies Channel99 and its separately published linear programme guide, alongside independently selected committee streams.
The parliamentary broadcast page identifies the TV channel separately from plenary and committee broadcasts.

timing_rules: Dates belong to the broadcaster day. Advance to the next calendar date only when a decreasing start clock exactly matches the preceding explicitly printed overnight end.
The31October22:00–00:00 row establishes1November for its following00:00 row; subsequent early-morning slots retain the advanced calendar date.
Do not infer programme ends or assign arbitrary DST folds. Missing/zero/ambiguous ends remain absent.
Source guide bounds remain source facts: do not create a seven-day rolling duration from channel-level availability.
language: Original titles are preserved. Programme audio language is not inferred from the script of the title.
validation: Real saved payloads and the shared scheduled HTTP transport both yield130 unique timed programmes, all accepted by quality assessment.
Official duplicate cards are collapsed only when metadata agrees; conflicts, stale calendars and malformed start clocks fail.
Source dates, Hebrew entity escaping, midnight continuity, DST gap/fold rejection, explicit source ends, missing ends and genuine empty tables have regression tests.
An independent read-only review reproduced130 programmes with0 overlaps.
remaining_holds: Separate committee-room feeds are not represented by this linear schedule.
This review does not change the existing permission status, media playback policy or IPTV admission rules.
